Q1.problem_type_and_essence: thin-structure fracture segmentation/detection under structured texture artifacts, with a label-budget deployment tradeoff

input_target_constraints.input: original unfolded borehole images; optional pixel/box labels
input_target_constraints.objective: recover true fractures while controlling texture/drilling/mud false positives
hard_constraints: do not rank methods only by visual examples
separate predictive quality from annotation/runtime deployment cost

baseline.name: Canny/ridge filter + morphology/connected-component cleanup
six_hour_plan: run Canny/line-ridge baseline with directional and component filters
hand-audit a small labeled subset or use available masks for IoU/F1
if labels are sufficient, add a compact U-Net baseline and compare on held-out images
baseline.why: no training and strong interpretability; directly tests whether labels/deep models are actually necessary

author_route.method: multi-feature K-Means, direction-enhanced Canny and YOLOv8 comparison; final practical recommendation is Canny + post-processing
why_fit: Canny is cheap and interpretable under limited annotation budget
YOLOv8 can learn complex appearance if high-quality labels exist
multi-feature classical cues can suppress texture
author_route.evidence_boundary: YOLOv8 is described as visually better in the body but no quantitative held-out metric is reported; appendix only shows a Canny fragment.

major_alternatives.why_can_work: pixel output matches task better than box-only detection
major_alternatives.when_prefer: enough independent pixel masks and stable held-out IoU/F1 gain
larger independent labeled set and compute budget

major_alternatives.model: YOLO segmentation rather than box detection
major_alternatives.why_can_work: learned object-level cues plus mask output
major_alternatives.when_prefer: annotation budget supports masks and classical false positives remain high

not_recommended.why_not_now: no quantitative independent comparison and labeling cost is the paper's own reason for rejecting it
leaks borehole texture and acquisition identity

Q2.problem_type_and_essence: instance grouping followed by constrained nonlinear geometric fitting of a periodic trace

input_target_constraints.decision: fracture instances and R,beta,C with known/fixed P where geometry permits
input_target_constraints.objective: low robust residual with physically plausible parameters
hard_constraints: period semantics fixed-vs-estimated must be explicit
cluster count must match actual instances or be model-selected
phase/amplitude canonicalization and reject state required

baseline.name: connected components/topology merge + bounded robust fixed-period least_squares
six_hour_plan: merge fragments by endpoint distance and tangent orientation
fix P=pi*D if borehole circumference is known
report R2, residual plots and rejected fits
baseline.why: directly solves the four-parameter geometry with far fewer degrees of freedom than a pseudo-neural optimizer

author_route.method: GMM grouping + gradient-descent/Newton hybrid vs no-hidden-layer linear neural parameterization optimized with Adam
why_fit: Newton-like local refinement can be fast near optimum
Adam can optimize differentiable sine parameters
author_route.evidence_boundary: printed appendix shows only GMM clustering; no GD/Newton or neural fitting code. R2 is evaluated on the same fitted traces and does not demonstrate cross-fracture generalization.

major_alternatives.why_can_work: unknown instance count and non-Gaussian curve-shaped clusters
major_alternatives.when_prefer: fragment count varies and curves are elongated/non-Gaussian

major_alternatives.why_can_work: soft assignment with roughly elliptical feature clusters
major_alternatives.when_prefer: cluster count can be selected by BIC and feature geometry is compatible

not_recommended.model: per-fracture no-hidden-layer 'neural network' as learned regressor
not_recommended.why_not_now: same-instance residual optimization does not create demonstrated transferable supervised learning and adds non-identifiable W,b around a single output vector

Q3.problem_type_and_essence: roughness estimation from an ordered physical profile under sampling-scale sensitivity

input_target_constraints.input: one fracture centerline/profile in physical coordinates
input_target_constraints.decision: raw roughness statistic and JRC under a canonical formula
input_target_constraints.objective: stable roughness estimate with sensitivity and calibration provenance
hard_constraints: profile must be ordered/single-valued for dy/dx-type estimator
one canonical JRC formula per registry

baseline.name: physical centerline + equal-arc-length sampling + official Z2/JRC + density sensitivity
six_hour_plan: extract ordered centerline rather than closed outer contour
convert x,y to consistent physical units
compute raw Z2/JRC across several sampling densities
baseline.why: transparent and exposes sampling dependence before adding an unvalidated second-derivative model

author_route.method: equal-spacing and curvature/compactness adaptive sampling plus second-derivative Z3 JRC improvement
why_fit: second derivative is sensitive to local bending
author_route.evidence_boundary: appendix implements neither adaptive sampling nor Z3/area correction; body switches JRC formulas and the claimed area correction is absent from the displayed improved equation.

major_alternatives.when_prefer: scale dependence is central and enough profiles exist for calibration

not_recommended.why_not_now: closed boundary can double back in x and violates single-valued profile assumptions

not_recommended.model: new Z3 coefficients without held-out calibration

Q4.problem_type_and_essence: 3D geometry inference plus uncertain connectivity scoring and active measurement placement

input_target_constraints.input: attachment-derived borehole coordinates, fracture-plane parameters, roughness and upstream uncertainties
input_target_constraints.decision: connectivity score/probability, uncertainty map, three feasible new boreholes
input_target_constraints.objective: reduce expected posterior uncertainty subject to geometry/engineering constraints
input_target_constraints.independent_evaluation_unit: fracture pair/network and candidate drilling site
hard_constraints: use real/declared scenario inputs with provenance
uncalibrated weighted score is not probability

baseline.name: geometry compatibility + bootstrap/Monte-Carlo uncertainty + feasible-grid expected information gain
six_hour_plan: compute transparent distance/orientation/depth compatibility and weight sensitivity
simulate/approximate observation outcomes and rank by expected entropy reduction
baseline.why: keeps uncertainty semantics and hard constraints explicit

author_route.method: weighted distance/orientation/JRC/depth score -> sigmoid 'probability'; voxel entropy; local-entropy 'information gain' drilling recommendation
why_fit: simple multi-factor fusion is easy to interpret
uncertainty hotspots are useful for active sampling
author_route.evidence_boundary: Q4 uses simulated/common-sense fracture inputs, binary entropy is incomplete, local prior entropy is not information gain, and one final recommended hole violates the stated 500 mm spacing.

major_alternatives.why_can_work: can produce calibrated probabilities if labeled/physics-simulation connectivity examples exist
honest when probability labels are unavailable
major_alternatives.when_prefer: only expert/geometry criteria exist; report weight sensitivity
spatial field representation and observation model are available

not_recommended.model: mean current entropy called information gain
not_recommended.why_not_now: does not model what a new observation will reveal or the posterior after observing it
can violate minimum spacing or cluster candidates
